title: End-to-end Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: Operational playbook that defines Redwood Inference's end-to-end processes for annual and quarterly budgeting, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, contract lifecycle and signatory rules, and revenue recognition and billing practices (high-level ASC 606 alignment and internal invoice/playbook flows).
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents the end-to-end operational processes for finance and legal activities that impact Redwood Inference's financial controls and customer-facing commercial flows. It combines budgeting & forecasting best practices with procurement and contract workflows and the revenue recognition & billing rules used by Finance and Legal. The goal is to ensure consistent execution, clear ownership, and auditability across the contract-to-cash and procure-to-pay lifecycles.

Scope:
- Budgeting & forecasting (annual, quarterly reforecasts, variance analysis)
- Procurement and vendor onboarding (low-touch to high-value purchases)
- Contract lifecycle (negotiation, approval, signature, storage)
- Revenue recognition & billing (ASC 606 alignment, invoice cadence, disputes)

Owners and primary contacts:
- Document owner: Finance (owner_team) - finance-legal
- Finance lead: Sofia Martinez (fp&a@redwood.example.com)
- Legal lead: Aisha Patel (legal@redwood.example.com)
- Procurement coordinator / AP: Liam O'Connor (procurement@redwood.example.com)
- ERP & Billing systems: NetSuite (billing), Stripe (payments), DocuSign (signatures)

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Summary:
Annual budgeting is the authoritative planning cycle; quarterly rolling forecasts provide ongoing alignment to operating realities. FP&A publishes a consolidated budget calendar and template each October for the next fiscal year.

Key artifacts and cadence:
- Annual operating plan (AOP) published by Finance in NetSuite and Confluence by Nov 30 each year.
- Quarterly reforecast windows: Q1 (Mar 15), Q2 (Jun 15), Q3 (Sep 15), Q4 (Dec 15).
- Monthly close: budget variance report delivered by 5th business day.

Owners and inputs:
- Product & Eng: headcount plans, infra and hosting spend, roadmap-driven investments
- Sales & GTM: ARR bookings targets, expected ramp schedules, seat-based pricing assumptions
- Research & Serving Runtime: capitalized infra projects (capex requests)
- Finance: consolidation, modeling, sensitivity analyses

Approval thresholds and routing:
- Ongoing operational spend within budget: team lead approval (no finance pre-approval required).
- Headcount hires: manager -> People Ops -> Finance (if >$250k annual run-rate -> Exec compensation committee).
- Capex requests >$50k: business lead -> Finance -> CFO sign-off.

Variance and performance monitoring:
- Scorecard metrics: ARR, Gross Margin, Cash Burn, Unit Cost per 1M tokens served, Infrastructure utilization %
- Actionable thresholds: If monthly burn deviates >10% vs forecast OR ARR bookings miss >7% -> mandatory cross-functional review within 5 business days.

2) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding

Purpose:
Standardize procurement to manage vendor risk, obtain competitive pricing, and ensure proper contractual controls.

Procurement tiers and approval matrix:
- Tier 1: Low-cost operational spend (<$5k) - Team lead approval, PO optional.
- Tier 2: Medium spend ($5k-$50k) - Procurement coordinator approval + 1 finance approver; create PO in NetSuite.
- Tier 3: High-value ($50k-$250k) - Procurement, Finance manager, Legal review for standard terms.
- Tier 4: Strategic (> $250k or multi-year commitments) - Procurement lead, Finance director, Legal counsel, and Exec sponsor. Board-level notification if contract materially impacts runway or strategy.

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum):
1. Completed Vendor Information Form (W-9 / W-8 + bank details)
2. Vendor risk assessment (security/compliance questionnaire) - if vendor handles customer data or PII, route to Security & Compliance for SOC2 evidence.
3. Standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) or approved contract template attached
4. Approved PO in NetSuite before work begins (except for pre-approved subscriptions).
5. Tax & payment setup in AP system; 3-way match enabled for goods/services.

Procurement steps (numbered):
1. Requestor raises an internal procurement request via the Procurement form (Confluence link) or procurement@redwood.example.com.
2. Procurement coordinator validates budget availability and assigns a procurement tier.
3. For Tier 2+, procurement sources vendor quotes (min 2 quotes recommended for >$25k).
4. Legal reviews contract language for Tier 3+ or any non-standard terms.
5. Finance issues PO in NetSuite and confirms payment terms.
6. Vendor signs contract (DocuSign) and returns fully executed copy.
7. Procurement closes request and uploads documentation to VendorCentral and Confluence reference page.

Sample procurement table (approval matrix):
| Spend band | Approvers required | Contract type | PO required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <$5k | Team lead | Subscription/one-off | Optional | Fast-track allowed |
| $5k-$50k | Procurement + Finance | Standard SOW or subscription | Yes | 2 vendor quotes encouraged |
| $50k-$250k | Procurement + Finance Mgr + Legal | MSA + SOW | Yes | Legal standard review |
| >$250k | Procurement Lead + Finance Dir + Legal + Exec | Strategic MSA | Yes | Exec sponsor & C-level sign-off |

3) Contract Lifecycle and Legal Process

Objective:
Ensure a repeatable and auditable contract lifecycle from initial commercial negotiation to signature, storage, and renewal.

Contract templates & routing:
- Approved templates: Sales MSA (rev 3.2), SaaS Subscription Addendum, Professional Services SOW, NDA (standard), Reseller Agreement. Templates are versioned and published in Confluence under /legal/templates.
- Non-standard clause flow: Any deviation from an approved template must be flagged in redline and include rationale. Legal will provide counter-proposal within 3 business days for Tier 1-2 deals; Tier 3+ may require Leadership review.

Signatory authority table:
- Sales contracts up to $500k ARR: VP Sales or delegated director with Finance countersignature.
- Contracts >$500k and <= $2M ARR: CFO + Legal.
- Contracts >$2M ARR or multi-year strategic commitments: CEO + CFO + Legal.
- Any contract that contains indemnity increases, non-standard data residency, or subprocessing must be reviewed by Head of Security & Legal and elevated to Execs as needed.

Contracting checklist (pre-signature):
1. Commercial summary (1-paragraph) with pricing, term, renewal cadence, termination & refund terms.
2. Legal redline and risk memo for material deviations.
3. Sales approval snapshot: ARR impact, onboarding plan, customer success owner.
4. Finance confirmation of revenue/billing treatment (preliminary revrec bucket).

Post-signature and storage:
- Fully executed contracts must be uploaded to Contract Repository (DocuSign storage + NetSuite reference + Confluence link) within 2 business days.
- Renewal notices: Salesforce/CPQ triggers renewal alerts 90/60/30 days prior; Legal/Account Exec to confirm renewal template.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing (high-level)

Principles and accounting policy alignment:
- Redwood follows ASC 606 principles: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- Finance maintains a set of RevRec buckets: SaaS (time-based), Professional Services (milestone or % complete), Credits & Refunds (contra revenue).

Common scenarios and treatment (examples):
- SaaS subscription (monthly/annual prepaid): Recognize ratably over the service period. Annual prepaid collected upfront is recorded as deferred revenue and amortized monthly.
- Usage-based billing (tokens/embeddings): Recognize when usage is recorded; monthly invoicing for prior period usage. Thresholds for estimates: if usage cannot be measured at period close, estimate based on prior periods and true-up on next invoice.
- Implementation services: If distinct and separately priced, recognized on completion of milestone; otherwise capitalize as contract asset and recognize over time using cost-to-cost method.

Billing cadence and systems:
- Invoicing systems: NetSuite generates invoices; Stripe processes card payments and recorded in NetSuite via automated connector.
- Billing cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or annual in advance for subscriptions (per contract).
- Payment terms: Standard = Net 30. Exceptions require Finance approval and are documented on contract. Late fees and collections policies are managed by AR team.

Revenue close controls and reconciliations:
- Monthly close checklist includes: deferred revenue roll-forward, contract adjustments, invoice-to-recognition reconciliation, and review of manual journal entries.
- Thresholds for manual review: any adjustment >$25k must include a supporting memo and be approved by Finance Director.

Disputes, credits, and chargebacks:
- Ticket the dispute in Salesforce with invoice reference and assign to AR & Sales.
- Temporary credit memos may be applied during dispute resolution but require CFO sign-off for credits >$10k.

5) Operational Playbooks and Runbooks (quick reference)

A. Creating a PO in NetSuite (5-step)
1. Log into NetSuite -> Procurement -> Create PO.
2. Link to vendor record; attach vendor W-9 and evidence.
3. Add budget code and attach Confluence Request ID.
4. Submit for approval; Finance will review within 2 business days.
5. After approval, send PO to vendor and store PO number in Contract Repository.

B. Contract signature (sales flow)
1. Confirm pricing and terms with customer; populate Sales MSA + Addendum.
2. Upload to DocuSign and set signing order: Customer -> VP Sales -> Finance (countersign) -> Legal (notice).
3. Once executed, save DocuSign PDF to Contract Repository and link in Salesforce opportunity.

C. Revenue recognition quick checks (monthly close)
- Verify deferred revenue roll-forward equals opening balance + cash collected - recognized revenue - refunds.
- Confirm usage-based revenue for prior month reconciles to internal metering (tokens served report).
- Flag reconciling items > $5k for manager review.

6) Controls, Auditability, and Records Retention

Record retention:
- Contracts: retain fully executed agreements for 7 years after expiration (electronic storage in Contract Repository).
- Invoices & receipts: retain for 7 years per tax and audit requirements.
- Vendor risk documentation and SOC2 evidence: retain for length of the vendor relationship + 3 years.

Internal controls and audit readiness:
- Access control: Document repositories and NetSuite require role-based access; Finance & Legal maintain access lists quarterly.
- Segregation of duties: Requestor -> Approver -> Payment should be distinct individuals. Approvers can't approve their own team expenses > $5k.
- Audit logs: NetSuite and DocuSign audit trails are exported to secure archive monthly and stored for internal audit.

7) Escalation paths and SLAs

SLA table (operational requests):
- Procurement request triage: 2 business days (procurement coordinator)
- Legal contract review (standard template): 3 business days
- Legal complex redline: 7-10 business days
- Billing dispute initial response: 3 business days

Escalation steps:
1. If an SLA is missed, procurement/finance/legal owner notifies FP&A and the requestor within 1 business day.
2. For high-impact items (>$250k or customer escalations), notify Director-level owner and include Exec sponsor.

Appendices

A. Sample contract clause checklist (must-haves)
- Clear description of services and deliverables
- Term, renewal, and termination clauses with notice windows
- Pricing schedule and invoicing cadence
- Confidentiality and data protection clauses aligned to Redwood's DPA
- Indemnification and liability caps (limit to 1x annual contract value where possible)

B. Templates & links
- Confluence: /legal/templates
- NetSuite PO playbook: /eng-finance/netsuite-playbook
- Vendor onboarding form: /finance-and-legal/vendor-onboarding-form

C. Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
Q: When can we start work with a vendor before a PO is issued?
A: Only for subscriptions and pre-approved vendors with existing POs. All other services require a PO before material work begins. Exceptions must be documented and approved by Finance.

Q: Who signs NDAs?
A: Standard mutual NDA may be signed by Director-level designee. Non-standard NDAs require Legal review.
